text:
For running, I'd start with the **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** if you want the best sound and can spend more, the **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** if hearing traffic matters most, or the **Soundcore AeroFit 2** or **JLab Flex Open** on a budget.

**Top picks**

1. **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (best overall).** Clip-on design with physical buttons, which reviewers find easier to use while running. Runner's World lists them at $199 (down from $299), and WIRED also lists $199 at Bose and Best Buy. They have 7 hours of battery and IPX4 water resistance. Drawbacks: they're expensive, and one reviewer found them too quiet in heavy traffic.
   - Sources: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/), [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

2. **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (best bone conduction).** Sends sound through your cheekbones and adds air-conduction speakers for bass. It has 12 hours of battery, USB-C charging, and an app with EQ. Runner's World lists it at $180, and WIRED lists $125 at REI and Best Buy. Drawbacks: the sound is less clear than the older OpenRun, and it can interfere with long hair, high ponytails, and hooded tops. Its IP55 rating means it's not for swimming.
   - Sources: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

3. **Shokz OpenDots 2 (best for long runs).** Clip-on earbuds with 10 hours per charge, 40 hours with the case, and IP57 rating. They're priced at $200. Like other open designs, they leak sound and don't block noise.
   - Sources: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

4. **Soundcore AeroFit 2 (best budget hook-style).** Open-ear hook design with 10 hours per bud, 42 hours with the case, IP55, and LDAC on Android. SoundGuys named it its best budget pick. Dealectric reports a 20% off code, AFSC20, that it tested on October 22, 2026. The code expires December 31, 2026, and excludes items already on sale. Prices conflict across sources: Dealectric lists $129.99 at Soundcore, while SoundGuys lists $79.99 at Amazon with a $99.99 MSRP. Check the price at checkout.
   - Buy: [Dealectric listing (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2). Dealectric earns a commission if you buy through it.
   - Sources: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2), [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

5. **JLab Flex Open (cheapest clip-on).** Runner's World lists it at $40, though its text says $50. It has 7 hours of battery, a volume-limiting safe-hearing setting, and touch-only controls. Expect less bass and detail than the pricier models.
   - Source: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Worth knowing**

- **Nothing Ear (Open)** is SoundGuys' pick for running. It's listed at $99 (down from $149) with IP54 rating and a parametric EQ. Source: [SoundGuys workout earbuds guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)
- Runner's World says Bose planned a new open-ear model around September 2026. I couldn't confirm whether it has launched, so check before buying the Ultra Open.
- Open-ear designs don't isolate sound, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

If you tell me your budget and whether you run on roads or trails, I can narrow this down.
